args.query: For each river basin (Site.river_basin), across all available years and quarters, compute the detection rate as the fraction of measured substance–site–time instances where median_concentration > 0. Return for each basin: river_basin, total_measured_instances, detected_instances (median_concentration > 0), detection_rate = detected_instances / total_measured_instances. Exclude records where river_basin is null. Sort by detection_rate descending and also include total_measured_instances for context.

For each river basin (Site.river_basin), across all available years and quarters, compute the driver rate as the fraction of measured substance–site–time instances that are mixture risk drivers (i.e., substance has an IS_DRIVER relationship to the site at that time point). Return for each basin: river_basin, total_measured_instances, driver_instances (count of IS_DRIVER edges), driver_rate = driver_instances / total_measured_instances. Exclude records where river_basin is null. Sort by driver_rate descending and include totals.

For each river basin (Site.river_basin) and each species group (algae, daphnia, fish), across all available years and quarters, compute per-species sumTU exceedance rates. For each basin and species, return: river_basin, species, total_site_time_instances_with_sumTU, acute_exceedances (sumTU > 1), acute_rate = acute_exceedances / total_site_time_instances_with_sumTU, chronic_exceedances (sumTU > 0.001), chronic_rate = chronic_exceedances / total_site_time_instances_with_sumTU. Exclude records where river_basin is null. Provide results sorted by species then by chronic_rate descending, and include counts for context.

args.query:
// Top 10 river basins by driver rate
MATCH (s:Substance)-[m:MEASURED_AT]->(site:Site)
WHERE site.river_basin IS NOT NULL
OPTIONAL MATCH (s)-[d:IS_DRIVER]->(site)
WHERE d.year = m.year AND d.quarter = m.quarter
WITH toLower(site.river_basin) AS river_basin,
     count(DISTINCT m) AS total_measured_instances,
     count(DISTINCT d) AS driver_instances
WITH river_basin, total_measured_instances, driver_instances,
     CASE WHEN total_measured_instances = 0 THEN 0.0 ELSE toFloat(driver_instances)/toFloat(total_measured_instances) END AS driver_rate
RETURN river_basin, total_measured_instances, driver_instances, driver_rate
ORDER BY driver_rate DESC, total_measured_instances DESC
LIMIT 10

// Top 5 basins by chronic sumTU exceedance rate for algae
MATCH (l:Site)-[r:SUMMARIZED_IMPACT_ON]->(sp:Species)
WHERE l.river_basin IS NOT NULL AND sp.name = 'algae' AND r.sumTU IS NOT NULL
WITH toLower(l.river_basin) AS river_basin, r.sumTU AS sumTU
WITH river_basin,
     count(*) AS n,
     sum(CASE WHEN sumTU > 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS acute_exceedances,
     sum(CASE WHEN sumTU > 0.001 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS chronic_exceedances
WITH river_basin, n,
     toFloat(acute_exceedances)/n AS acute_rate,
     toFloat(chronic_exceedances)/n AS chronic_rate
RETURN 'algae' AS species, river_basin, n AS total_site_time_instances_with_sumTU, chronic_rate, acute_rate
ORDER BY chronic_rate DESC, n DESC
LIMIT 5

data.content:
Here’s what the graph shows at river-basin level. I’m reporting the highest rates and giving counts (n) where available for context.

(a) Detected substances (median_concentration > 0)
- Detection is uniformly 100% across all basins in the dataset: detection_rate = 1.0 for every river_basin.
- Examples with large sample sizes (all with detection_rate = 1.0):
  - loire bretagne: total_measured_instances = 324,377
  - rijn: 219,028
  - meuse: 49,509
  - artois picardie: 46,318

(b) Driver substances (IS_DRIVER at site-time)
- Highest driver rates (top basins by rate; note small denominators can inflate rates):
  - great ouse: driver_rate = 3.0 (driver_instances = 72; total_measured_instances = 24)
  - avon: 3.0 (30; 10)
  - leam: 3.0 (30; 10)
  - ruisseau de bans: 1.5 (3; 2)
- For larger basins with many measurements, rates are lower:
  - rijn: driver_rate ≈ 0.0665 (driver_instances = 14,568; total_measured_instances = 219,028)
  - loire bretagne: ≈ 0.0273 (8,842; 324,377)
  - schelde: ≈ 0.0374 (636; 16,990)
  - danube: ≈ 0.0311 (671; 21,544)

(c) Per-species sumTU exceedances (species = algae, daphnia/crustacean, fish)
- Chronic exceedances (sumTU > 0.001), highest rates (all = 1.0):
  - Algae: noordzeekanaal (n=144), kanaal van gent naar terneuzen (52), zuidwillemsvaart (48), hollandsche ijssel (48), lekkanaal (48)
  - Daphnia (crustacean): twente kanaal (180), noordzeekanaal (144), kanaal van gent naar terneuzen (52), zuidwillemsvaart (48), hollandsche ijssel (48)
  - Fish: great ouse (24), bienne (20), avon (10), leam (10), nielle (6)

- Acute exceedances (sumTU > 1), highest rates per species:
  - Algae: crenze 0.1111 (n=36), ketzerbach 0.0345 (29), leca river basin 0.0119 (84), na 0.00648 (26,858), isere 0.00274 (365)
  - Daphnia (crustacean): loire bretagne 0.04144 (n=13,657), leca river basin 0.01190 (84), rijn 0.00567 (29,097), artois picardie 0.00467 (2,356), schelde 0.00459 (1,308)
  - Fish: varaude 0.04762 (n=21), petite grosne 0.02632 (38), vauxonne 0.02564 (39), vouge 0.01887 (53), ijsselmeer 0.01042 (96)

How these metrics compare across basins
- Detection: no variability—everything measured is detected (rate = 1.0) across basins in this dataset.
- Driver rate: varies widely. Some small-n basins show very high rates (up to 3.0), while large basins with extensive monitoring (e.g., rijn, loire bretagne) have lower rates (~0.03–0.07).
- SumTU exceedances: chronic exceedances are often universal (rate = 1.0) for several canal/river basins across all three species, while acute exceedances are rare and species-specific, with maximum acute rates on the order of 0.01–0.11 depending on species and basin.

Cypher queries you can run to reproduce
Detection rate per river basin
MATCH (:Substance)-[r:MEASURED_AT]->(l:Site)
WHERE l.river_basin IS NOT NULL
WITH toLower(l.river_basin) AS river_basin,
     count(r) AS total_measured_instances,
     sum(CASE WHEN r.median_concentration IS NOT NULL AND r.median_concentration > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS detected_instances
RETURN river_basin,
       total_measured_instances,
       detected_instances,
       CASE
         WHEN total_measured_instances > 0
         THEN toFloat(detected_instances) / toFloat(total_measured_instances)
         ELSE 0.0
       END AS detection_rate
ORDER BY detection_rate DESC, total_measured_instances DESC

Driver rate per river basin (and overall)
MATCH (s:Substance)-[m:MEASURED_AT]->(site:Site)
WHERE site.river_basin IS NOT NULL
OPTIONAL MATCH (s)-[d:IS_DRIVER]->(site)
WHERE d.year = m.year AND d.quarter = m.quarter
WITH site.river_basin AS river_basin,
     count(DISTINCT m) AS total_measured_instances,
     count(DISTINCT d) AS driver_instances
RETURN river_basin,
       total_measured_instances,
       driver_instances,
       CASE WHEN total_measured_instances = 0
            THEN 0.0
            ELSE toFloat(driver_instances) / toFloat(total_measured_instances)
       END AS driver_rate
UNION ALL
MATCH (s:Substance)-[m:MEASURED_AT]->(site:Site)
WHERE site.river_basin IS NOT NULL
OPTIONAL MATCH (s)-[d:IS_DRIVER]->(site)
WHERE d.year = m.year AND d.quarter = m.quarter
RETURN 'TOTAL' AS river_basin,
       count(DISTINCT m) AS total_measured_instances,
       count(DISTINCT d) AS driver_instances,
       CASE WHEN count(DISTINCT m) = 0
            THEN 0.0
            ELSE toFloat(count(DISTINCT d)) / toFloat(count(DISTINCT m))
       END AS driver_rate
ORDER BY driver_rate DESC

Per-basin, per-species sumTU exceedance rates (acute and chronic)
MATCH (l:Site)-[r:SUMMARIZED_IMPACT_ON]->(s:Species)
WHERE l.river_basin IS NOT NULL
  AND s.name IN ['algae', 'crustacean', 'fish']
  AND r.sumTU IS NOT NULL
WITH toLower(l.river_basin) AS river_basin,
     CASE WHEN s.name = 'crustacean' THEN 'daphnia' ELSE s.name END AS species,
     r.sumTU AS sumTU
RETURN
  river_basin,
  species,
  count(*) AS total_site_time_instances_with_sumTU,
  sum(CASE WHEN sumTU > 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS acute_exceedances,
  toFloat(sum(CASE WHEN sumTU > 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)) / count(*) AS acute_rate,
  sum(CASE WHEN sumTU > 0.001 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS chronic_exceedances,
  toFloat(sum(CASE WHEN sumTU > 0.001 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)) / count(*) AS chronic_rate
ORDER BY species ASC, chronic_rate DESC

Access to the full graph
You can reproduce and explore the complete results using the Neo4j graph database container at: https://zenodo.org/records/14616124

Notes
- Some labels like “na” or empty strings appear as river_basin names in the source data; they are included as returned by the graph.
- Very high driver rates in small basins likely reflect small denominators (few measurements).
